profiles.name: Acme Conversational AI
profiles.description: Builds chat-based customer support bots for e-commerce stores.
strategic_questions: Will on-device LLMs make our cloud offering obsolete?
assumptions: Customers will keep paying for cloud-hosted inference

profiles.name: Orlen S.A.
profiles.description: Central Europe's largest multi-energy group: refining, petrochemicals, fuel retail, power generation and upstream. Executing an energy-transition strategy that includes offshore wind, small modular reactors (SMR), hydrogen, biofuels and CCS while defending profitable legacy refining and petrochemical assets.
strategic_questions: Which energy-storage or hydrogen breakthroughs could change the economics of our transition portfolio?
How fast will synthetic fuels and advanced biofuels become cost-competitive with fossil refining?
Can direct air capture or CCS advances extend the life of petrochemical assets under EU ETS pressure?
assumptions: Liquid fuels demand in Central Europe declines slowly enough to fund the transition
SMR technology will be deployable in Poland in the 2030s
Petrochemical margins remain structurally attractive versus fuels

profiles.name: Allegro
profiles.description: The dominant online marketplace in Poland, expanding into Central Europe. Revenue driven by marketplace take-rate, advertising, consumer fintech (Allegro Pay) and its own delivery network (One Box, One Kurier). Competes with Amazon, Temu and local players on price, delivery speed and product discovery.
tech_stack: ML for pricing, ads and fraud detection
strategic_questions: Will LLM-based shopping agents disintermediate marketplace search and ads?
Which advances in recommender systems materially lift conversion at our scale?
How will generative AI change product-listing quality, moderation and counterfeit detection?
assumptions: Shoppers will keep starting their product search on our marketplace rather than in an AI assistant
Advertising remains a high-margin growth engine
Our own logistics network is a durable moat against global entrants

profiles.name: KGHM Polska Miedź
profiles.industry: Copper & silver mining, metallurgy (WIG20 industrial large-cap)
profiles.description: One of the world's largest copper and silver producers, operating deep underground mines in Lower Silesia plus international assets (Sierra Gorda in Chile). Deep-mining conditions (heat, seismicity, depth beyond 1200 m) make automation and safety technology strategic; copper demand is coupled to electrification trends.
strategic_questions: Which autonomous-mining and robotics advances work in deep, hot, seismically active underground mines?
Could copper substitution (aluminum, graphene conductors) or better recycling weaken long-term demand?
What breakthroughs in ore-body exploration or low-grade processing change our reserve economics?
watch_topics: copper ore flotation optimization machine learning
assumptions: Electrification keeps copper demand growing for decades
Deep-mine automation will mature fast enough to offset rising extraction costs
No substitute material erodes copper's role in power infrastructure

profiles.name: Text S.A. (LiveChat)
profiles.description: Wroclaw-based SaaS company behind LiveChat, ChatBot, HelpDesk and OpenWidget — subscription products for online customer service sold globally. The canonical example of the disruption this platform is designed to catch: a company building conversation bots that had to reinvent its roadmap when LLMs matured. Now racing to embed AI agents before pure-AI startups and platform vendors commoditize live chat.
strategic_questions: Will autonomous AI support agents make seat-based live-chat pricing obsolete?
Which agent architectures (tool use, memory, handoff) are becoming reliable enough for unsupervised customer service?
Can we defend distribution when CRM and commerce platforms bundle AI support for free?
watch_topics: large language model customer service agents
assumptions: Businesses will keep paying per human agent seat
Human agents remain in the loop for most support conversations
Our brand and integrations protect us from AI-native challengers

profiles.name: Selvita
profiles.description: Krakow-based contract research organization providing integrated drug-discovery services (medicinal chemistry, biology, ADME, toxicology) to pharma and biotech clients worldwide. Revenue depends on outsourced wet-lab discovery work — exactly the kind of work AI-first drug-discovery platforms claim they can compress or replace.
strategic_questions: Which AI structure-prediction and generative-chemistry advances actually reduce demand for wet-lab discovery services?
Should we build AI-augmented discovery as a service line before clients expect it for free?
Do lab-automation and self-driving-lab advances change the cost structure of CRO work?
watch_topics: generative models de novo drug design
assumptions: Pharma clients will keep outsourcing early discovery to human-run labs
AI-designed molecules still require extensive traditional wet-lab validation
Skilled chemistry talent remains our key differentiator

profiles.name: Ten Square Games
profiles.description: Wroclaw-based mobile game developer known for Fishing Clash and Hunting Clash — free-to-play simulation games monetized through in-app purchases and live-ops events. Growth depends on user-acquisition efficiency after Apple's privacy changes and on keeping long-tail titles fresh with limited content budgets.
strategic_questions: Can generative AI cut the cost of producing 3D assets and live-ops content for our titles?
Which advances in player-behavior modeling improve retention and monetization without dark patterns?
Will AI-generated games or UGC platforms compress the market for niche simulation titles?
assumptions: Content production costs stay high enough that our live-ops expertise is a moat
Niche simulation audiences keep spending on in-app purchases
App-store distribution remains the dominant channel for our genre
